rv.q: Owen’s glittering eyes as he inhales the fumes of righteous certainty, Charly’s rapt face and stone-still form as she watches her brother, reaching for the light, walking toward the dark — both are some of the most haunting images I’ve seen onstage this year.
I was caught utterly off guard by this show, by its confidence and heft.
Thanks to the talented cast, the characters’ frustration does not become the audience’s frustration.

cn.t: Critics largely rave about Dan Giles's "The Charioteer," calling it assured and heartbreaking, with standout performances from its two leads. One outlier finds it uneven, but the consensus marks it as a compelling anticapitalist parable.
